title: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2 reach silver-medal standard on IMO 2024 problems, graded by two IMO gold medallists; IMO-certified gold follows in 2025
summary: DeepMind AI scored 28/42 on IMO 2024 problems, graded by Gowers and Myers; Gemini Deep Think's 35/42 in 2025 was IMO-certified gold
account: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof (reinforcement learning over the Lean proof language) and AlphaGeometry 2 produced solutions to four of the six 2024 International Mathematical Olympiad problems. Because the systems work in formal language, the problems were first translated manually into Lean. One problem was solved within minutes and others took up to three days, longer than the contest allows. Two former IMO gold medalists, Sir Timothy Gowers and Joseph Myers, graded the solutions under IMO rules. They awarded 28 of 42 points, a silver-medal score. DeepMind announced the result on 25 July 2024 (grading date not given). In July 2025 a Gemini Deep Think model working in natural language within the time limit scored 35 of 42. IMO president Gregor Dolinar confirmed this as a gold-medal score. Nature reported that OpenAI also claimed a gold-level result.
purpose: Solve competition mathematics problems with machine-checkable formal proofs
model_version: AlphaProof (2024) and AlphaGeometry 2; 2025 echo: advanced Gemini Deep Think
taxonomy_note: A graded competition score is read as task performance; no deployment or user is involved.

ratings.reason: A capability evaluation on IMO 2024 problems for the developer and the IMO community. The sources describe grading and scores, not a deployment or an observed organizational change.
Proofs of already-solved contest problems graded correct, with no identifiable beneficiary beyond the research community. Scientific American notes around 60 students scored better in 2024.

ai_role.statement: The AI systems produced the proofs. Humans manually formalized the 2024 problem statements into Lean (Scientific American) and graded the output. In 2024 the solutions were graded by two mathematicians at DeepMind's request (one of them, Myers, chaired the IMO 2024 Problem Selection Committee). The result was not officially certified by the IMO. DeepMind states the 2025 result was graded and certified by IMO coordinators, with the IMO president's confirmation appearing in the vendor blog. The cited sources do not state whether OpenAI's 2025 claim was certified by the IMO.
